title: Rapid User Researcher
description:
Who We Are
Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.
Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.
About The Role
We’re seeking a
Rolling User Researcher (Rolling UXR)
to deliver fast, high-signal insights that improve Notion’s product experiences across Product, Design, and Engineering (EPD)—including
AI-powered workflows
like Notion custom agents and chat. This is a
tactical, high-velocity
role: you’ll run lightweight usability and concept tests on a steady cadence, identify what’s not working, and help teams translate feedback into concrete product changes. Besides conducting research, you’ll also build and scale a program that makes it easy for product teams to submit testing requests and easy for you to recruit participants, along with a prioritization framework that helps you focus on the most important work.
This role is ideal for a researcher who loves the craft of moderated testing, can context-switch across many teams, and thrives in a “many small studies” model.
This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.
What You'll Achieve
End-to-end tactical research: Scope, design, and execute quick-turn research across the product lifecycle—delivering clear recommendations that drive product decisions, including
Rolling usability testing: Plan and moderate rapid usability tests on prototypes and in-product flows; identify friction, comprehension gaps, and failure points; recommend practical fixes and prototype them with AI.
Concept testing: Help teams evaluate early ideas (storyboards, low/high-fidelity prototypes, new IA) to understand desirability, comprehension, and expected workflows—before teams invest heavily in build.
Research pipeline ownership: Keep an always-on motion healthy by managing intake/prioritization, study cadence, participant recruitment, and consistent output formats so partners know what to expect and can act quickly.
Communication: Deliver crisp, actionable recommendation (severity, confidence, recommended next steps) in the right format for the audience—async write-ups, clips, or working sessions.
Business-minded impact: Connect findings to outcomes—why an issue matters, what to change, and what to watch—then follow through with teams to ensure improvements land.
Skills You'll Need To Bring
Research craft: You can independently run usability and/or concept tests end-to-end (scoping → protocol → moderation → synthesis → readout), and you know how to keep scope tight while preserving rigor. You’re also comfortable using AI thoughtfully to speed up prep/synthesis while maintaining quality and traceability to evidence.
AI fluency: You’re curious and hands-on with AI products and can translate concepts, like trust, usefulness, tone, safety, and clarity, into observable behaviors and research questions.
Pragmatism + speed: You excel at prioritizing in fast-moving environments, are comfortable with ambiguity, and can deliver quality research quickly with transparent limitations.
Systems thinking: You can quickly understand complex user journeys and identify where experiences break down across the system—from inputs, to product behavior, to UI patterns.
Communication: You write clearly, facilitate effectively, and can translate messy data into decisions and next steps for busy EPD partners.
Collaboration: You’re comfortable working across many stakeholders and switching context quickly without dropping details.
Experience: 3+ years of hands-on UX research experience (industry, agency, or equivalent)
Nice To Haves
Familiarity with AI-enabled product experiences (e.g., assistants/agents) and how to evaluate workflow success, user expectations, and trust.
Comfort collaborating on research-operations basics (recruiting, scheduling, etc.) to keep a rolling cadence healthy.
Background in UX design, engineering, or similar.

The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in San Francisco or New York City, the estimated base salary range for this role is $164,000-$190,000 per year.
By clicking “Submit Application”, I understand and agree that Notion and its affiliates and subsidiaries will collect and process my information in accordance with Notion’s Global Recruiting Privacy Policy and NYLL 144.
A Note on AI
You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.
Equal Opportunity & Accommodations

title: Intermediate User Researcher
description:
About The Role
Hippo Digital is recruiting for intermediate consultants in user research. User researchers design, plan and conduct research into what people need from a service and produce recommendations for user-centred service design. Working with designers, product owners, developers and other members of Agile teams, you will also test services as they are being designed and use research evidence to help explain design decisions to clients.
As an intermediate consultant in user research, you’ll come to Hippo with strong user research skills and some experience of advising others on how to design user-centred services. Support usability evaluation sessions
Use a range of tools to collect data, and write research reports to present findings
Effectively present your findings and related design/business recommendations and customer insights to stakeholders
Collaborate with other members of Agile, multidisciplinary teams within a user-centred design process
Learn from insights from user research and metrics to define and improve the service, and explain your decisions clearly
Run workshops with your team and stakeholders
Work with the Hippo research and design community to share best practice
About The Candidate
Experience of working with senior stakeholders
Experience of using different research methods (qualitative and quantitative) to gain insights
Working knowledge of user-centred design principles and practices
Understanding of a client’s strategic objectives and how the insights from your research support them
Ability to explain your findings and deal with challenges from stakeholders
About The Company

Hi, we’re Hippo
At Hippo, we design with empathy and build for impact. We do this by combining data-informed evidence, human-centred design and software engineering. We're a digital services partner who is genuinely invested in helping our clients thrive as modern organisations. Our delivery methodology is truly agile, from concept to reality, supporting innovation and continuous improvement to achieve your desired outcomes.
We firmly believe that technology should serve humanity, not the other way around. About Fulfillment IQ (FIQ):
Fulfillment IQ is a supply chain engineering and transformation company that helps brands, retailers, and 3PLs design, build, and scale high-performance logistics operations.
We work at the intersection of strategy, operations, and technology where we solve complex, real-world problems across warehouse design, automation, order management, transportation, and end-to-end supply chain execution.
Our teams combine deep domain expertise with strong technical capability, delivering outcomes through consulting, systems implementation, and proprietary platforms that accelerate time-to-value and reduce delivery risk.
If you enjoy working in complex environments, partnering closely with clients, and seeing your work make a tangible impact on how global commerce moves, this is the place where your skills and judgment truly come to life.
Role Overview
We're looking for a mid-level UI/UX Designer to join Crossdock Studios, where we specialize in bringing 0-to-1 product ideas to life. You'll work across the full design lifecycle — from early concept and user research through wireframes, prototypes, and polished, production-ready UI — partnering closely with product managers and engineers to turn ambiguous, early-stage ideas into simple, intuitive experiences.
This is a generalist role: you'll move fluidly between research, interaction design, visual design, and design systems work, depending on what the product needs at any given moment. You'll thrive here if you enjoy the challenge of designing for products that don't exist yet.
What You'll Do:
Research & Discovery: Conduct user interviews, synthesize findings, and translate insights into actionable design decisions
UX Design: Map user journeys and flows, build wireframes and prototypes, and iterate based on feedback and usability testing
UI Design: Create polished, high-fidelity mockups and visual designs that are consistent, accessible, and on-brand
Design Systems: Contribute to and maintain a shared component library/design system to ensure consistency across web and mobile
Collaboration: Partner closely with PMs and engineers throughout the product lifecycle — from early concept through implementation and QA
Prototyping: Build interactive prototypes to test concepts before development investment
Cross-functional Communication: Present design rationale and decisions clearly to stakeholders, incorporating feedback from technical and non-technical partners alike
What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days:
30 Days In
Ramped up on Crossdock's product portfolio, current design system, and existing Figma libraries/component patterns
Shadowed active projects to understand how the team moves from research through to shipped UI, and met the cross-functional partners (Product, Engineering, Marketing)
Completed at least one small, well-scoped design task (e.g., a UI polish pass or a minor flow update) to get familiar with the review and handoff process
60 Days In
Independently owned the design for one feature or workflow end-to-end — from wireframes through high-fidelity UI — with light oversight from Linda
Started contributing to the shared component library/design system rather than only consuming it
Built working relationships with engineering (comfortable handing off specs that a developer can build from without repeated clarification)
90 Days In
Leading design on a defined product area or workstream with minimal day-to-day oversight, including running or synthesizing user research when needed
Demonstrated ability to balance multiple in-flight design requests across Product, Engineering, and Marketing stakeholders
Design output is consistently meeting Linda's bar for quality without requiring significant rework
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):
Design throughput: Number of features/flows taken from concept to shipped UI per quarter
Design system contribution: Number of components added to or improved in the shared library
Cycle time: Time from design kickoff to engineering-ready handoff, and reduction in handoff rework/clarification cycles
Stakeholder satisfaction: Qualitative feedback from Product and Engineering partners on clarity and usability of design handoffs
Usability quality: Results from usability testing/feedback cycles on shipped designs (e.g., reduced friction points identified post-launch)
Requirements
What We're Looking For:
3-5 years of experience in UI/UX design for digital products (web and/or mobile)
A strong portfolio demonstrating end-to-end design work — research, flows, wireframes, prototypes, and finished UI
Proficiency with Figma and experience creating interactive prototypes for validation
Solid understanding of usability principles and accessibility standards
Experience contributing to or maintaining a design system
Experience working in fast-moving B2B or SaaS product environments
Eligible to work in Canada
Nice to Have:
Experience leveraging AI tools to accelerate design work — e.g., using AI for generating mockups, building out or maintaining design systems, speeding up iteration, or exploring concepts faster and with higher quality
Experience designing for complex, data-rich, or workflow-driven products (e.g., internal tools, enterprise software, dashboards) is a plus
Knowledge of responsive design best practices is a plus
Benefits

At Fulfillment IQ, we don't just build supply chain solutions. We build careers, friendships, and unforgettable experiences.
We believe in giving our senior technical leaders real ownership, real influence, and the opportunity to shape platforms that power real-world logistics operations.
As an equal opportunity employer, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all team members.

Build systems that directly impact global commerce and supply chain performance.

We invest in mentorship, leadership development, learning budgets, and long-term career growth.
Flexibility to Thrive
We support hybrid work models to help you perform at your best.

From team wins to work anniversaries, we recognize impact, celebrate milestones and reward performance.

Work alongside talented engineers, product leaders, and award-winning domain experts who value ownership, transparency, and high standards.

title: UI/UX Designer
description:
We want you to #JOINTHEREBELLION!
For 30 years we've been independently developing and publishing incredible video games at our multiple studios founded by Jason & Chris Kingsley, but Rebellion is more than just games. We have our own film studio, we create board games, publish books, and through 2000AD, publish comics and graphic novels such as the amazing Judge Dredd.
We are seeking a mid-level UI/UX Designer to join our dynamic UI/UX team, where you will have the chance to influence a variety of exciting, yet-to-be-announced projects. This is your opportunity to become part of a studio renowned for the Sniper Elite series and fresh from the success of Atomfall, our biggest game launch to date.
Your job will be to solve complex UX problems for a new project. You will work with game designers and UI artists to create intuitive UI designs, helping to implement these in game using a visual scripting tool set.
You will be skilled with wireframing and prototyping tools and be comfortable using a UX methodology to both define and solve player problems. You will be comfortable working to an existing style guide and be able to translate your ideas into high fidelity art targets using the Adobe suite.
As part of the UI team, you will play a key role in implementing efficient, complex, and beautiful UI, working with multiple disciplines with different experiences from different walks of life. We believe that UI is never solved by a single person or a single point of view and that is why we want the best collaborators so that we can work together to make memorable experiences for us and for our players!
This role is based at our riverside headquarters in Oxford, offering a creative and relaxed atmosphere where teamwork drives our success. We can provide a relocation package, including moving assistance, temporary accommodation, and full support to ensure a smooth transition to your new environment.
Responsibilities
:
Design multi-platform UI solutions for a variety of input devices
Define and mentor team on best practices and principles within the industry
Collaborate with Design and UI Art to create wireframes, high-fidelity mock-ups and prototypes
Identify and clearly define complex UX problems before moving into solution design
Recognise benefits, risks, costs and feasibility of project features in order to find achievable solutions
Learn to use a visual scripting tool set to implement your solutions yourself
Champion usability and accessibility
Welcome a diverse set of viewpoints from multiple teams, encouraging collaboration wherever possible
Research and solve any UI barriers for players through iteration based on internal feedback
Assist with optimisation and debugging to fix the issues raised by testers
Requirements
Experience in a similar role
Portfolio of interaction design showing awareness of UX methodology, wireframing and prototyping
Portfolio of visual design showing fundamental awareness of hierarchy, typography and composition
Experience championing the player's perspective, reducing cognitive load and building consistency across a product.
Desire to learn to implement in engine using a similar visual scripting toolset like Unreal or Unity UMG
Benefits
We offer an extensive benefits package to our team including:
22 days holidays + Christmas closure (typically 4 days) & Bank holidays (increasing with service at 5 years - one day each year until you reach 31 days)
Private Medical Insurance, healthcare cash plan, including dental and Vision
Life Assurance, Income Protection & Critical Illness Cover
Enhanced Family Leave
Interest Free, Tax-Free loans
Enhanced Pension Scheme
EAP a range of Mental Health and Wellbeing Support
Plus loads more... including a wide range of discounts, freebies, and social events!
Right to Work Statement
This role is only open to applicants who have the permanent right to work in the UK. We are unable to provide or take over visa sponsorship, either now or in the future. Applicants must therefore be able to demonstrate their ongoing eligibility to work in the UK without the need for employer sponsorship.
Life at Our Oxford HQ
Our riverside headquarters in Oxford places you a short walk away from the city centre. Renowned for its rich historical backdrop and esteemed educational institutions, Oxford offers a unique blend of tradition and modernity, with its beautiful architecture and green spaces.
Oxford also boasts excellent transport links, making it easy to navigate both the city and the wider country. The city's train station, just a short walk from our studio, offers frequent services to London, as well as direct routes to major cities like Birmingham, Manchester, and Reading and we also offer free parking at the studio.
Our open-plan office promotes teamwork and innovation, with regular interaction with senior management and other departments, alongside access to free hot drinks, a handy tuck shop onsite and a range of local pubs, cafes and dining options nearby helping make every workday enjoyable!
Inside Rebellion
Whichever team you join at Rebellion we are proud of our open, friendly, and creative atmosphere. We love what we do, and we have fun doing it! As a big indie developer, we have complete creative freedom over our titles which allows us to work on a massive variety of projects across all the major platforms.
Find out more about us
here
Our size, stability, and the variety of in-house expertise across multiple industries, makes Rebellion completely unique! We work in our own way, and we celebrate that as the key to our success. We foster an inclusive culture where you are encouraged to be yourself, to express your creativity and your talent. We are people focused and will support you in every way to can be the best at what you do. We recognise the importance of enjoying what you do and having a healthy work-life balance. We offer a friendly, creative, and relaxed working atmosphere, with sensibly managed projects and a wide variety of benefits and development opportunities for all our teams to ensure you are fully supported with your physical and Mental Well-being.
We are actively recruiting for a diverse team and continue to add to our culture of growth and inclusion. Rebellion encourages innovation in all areas, and we look forward to hearing how you can help us to be better. We encourage all demographics of culture, gender, ethnicity, neurodiversity and beyond, because a representative team makes better products.
If you are interested in working at Rebellion, but this role doesn't sound quite like you, we're recruiting for a range of positions across the studio and we're always happy to receive speculative applications via our website. Visit our Careers website to view all our live vacancies: Rebellion: Careers

H&R Block fosters a workplace in which individual differences are recognized, appreciated and respected. title: AI Product Designer
description:
We help the world run better
At SAP, we keep it simple: you bring your best to us, and we'll bring out the best in you. We're builders touching over 20 industries and 80% of global commerce, and we need your unique talents to help shape what's next. The work is challenging – but it matters. You'll find a place where you can be yourself, prioritize your wellbeing, and truly belong. What's in it for you? Constant learning, skill growth, great benefits, and a team that wants you to grow and succeed.
Role Overview
As an AI Product Designer, you will turn product vision, user needs, and business requirements into clear and intuitive experiences for SAP’s internal AI products, tools, and platforms.
You will work across the full design process, from research and early concepts through prototyping, validation, implementation, and launch communication. You will partner closely with Product Managers, Engineers, AI specialists, and business stakeholders to simplify complex workflows and create solutions that are useful, scalable, and aligned with SAP design standards.
This is a multidisciplinary role combining product design, UX research, interaction and visual design, motion design, branding, and product communication. Product design is the core of the role, supported by strong visual storytelling and communication skills.
What You'll Do
Product Design and Delivery
Own the design of new products, features, and functional modules from early exploration through implementation and iteration.
Lead the end-to-end UX/UI process, including research, user flows, wireframes, prototyping, visual design, validation, and developer handover.
Translate complex AI capabilities, technical constraints, and business requirements into clear and intuitive user experiences.
Develop user journeys, service blueprints, information architecture, and experience maps where needed.
Work with Product and Engineering to assess trade-offs, shape product direction, and ensure the final implementation reflects the intended experience.
Review implemented designs and help resolve usability, accessibility, visual, and interaction issues before release.
AI Experience Design
Design AI-enabled experiences such as conversational interfaces, assisted workflows, recommendations, automation, and human-in-the-loop interactions.
Consider how users understand and respond to uncertainty, loading, errors, fallbacks, and AI-generated outputs.
Create clear ways for users to review, edit, approve, correct, or override AI-generated results.
Apply responsible design principles, including transparency, privacy, accessibility, user control, and appropriate human oversight.
Explore new interaction models such as agentic, multimodal, and adaptive experiences when relevant to the product.
Research and Product Strategy
Plan and conduct user interviews, surveys, usability tests, and validation sessions, then translate the findings into practical design recommendations.
Use qualitative feedback and product data to identify friction, prioritise improvements, and support ongoing iteration.
Facilitate design thinking, co-creation, and stakeholder workshops to frame problems, generate ideas, and align teams around a direction.
Contribute a user-centred design perspective to product strategy, roadmap discussions, and prioritisation.
Design Systems and Content
Create and maintain reusable components, patterns, and visual systems aligned with SAP Fiori and SAP design standards.
Help define reusable patterns for AI interactions, responsive behaviour, motion, and common system states.
Maintain consistency across typography, colour, imagery, layout, and interface behaviour.
Write or contribute to interface copy, prompts, guidance, empty states, error messages, and onboarding content.
Build accessibility and inclusive design into the design and review process.
Motion, Branding, and Product Communication
Create product identities, visual assets, illustrations, and communication materials that are distinctive while remaining aligned with SAP’s corporate identity.
Define and maintain a consistent visual direction across product interfaces, presentations, launch materials, and other communication touchpoints.
Produce product walkthroughs, interface demonstrations, feature videos, launch content, and motion graphics using tools such as Adobe After Effects.
Use motion and storytelling to explain complex capabilities, demonstrate product value, and support product adoption.
Design interface animations and transitions that clarify system behaviour and guide user attention.
What You Bring
2 to 5 years of proven experience in product design, UX/UI design, interaction design, and motion design.
A strong portfolio showing end-to-end product design work, including research, user flows, prototypes, visual systems, and implemented products.
High proficiency in Figma, including prototyping, component creation, and design-system management.
Strong visual and UI design skills, with good judgement in typography, layout, hierarchy, consistency, and interaction details.
Experience designing complex enterprise, SaaS, platform, or workflow-based products.
High proficiency in Adobe After Effects, with experience creating product animations, interface demonstrations, or feature videos.
Experience in branding and art direction, including product identities, logos, visual assets, and communication systems.
Practical experience conducting UX research, usability testing, and user validation.
A strong understanding of interaction design, usability, accessibility, and human-centred design.
Familiarity with AI-powered products and the design challenges associated with generative AI, conversational interfaces, automation, and intelligent recommendations.
Ability to work independently, manage several design workstreams, and take projects from ambiguity to delivery.
Experience facilitating workshops and working with diverse stakeholders to turn discussions into clear design decisions.
Strong communication and storytelling skills, including the ability to explain design decisions and influence stakeholders.
Experience working closely with Product Managers, Engineers, researchers, and other cross-functional partners.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience designing generative AI, conversational, agentic, multimodal, or automation-based products.
Experience working on internal enterprise tools or platforms serving multiple user groups.
Familiarity with SAP Fiori, SAP design standards, or another established enterprise design system.
Knowledge of accessibility standards such as WCAG 2.2 AA.
Basic understanding of HTML, CSS, front-end frameworks, or design-to-development workflows.
Additional experience in video editing, illustration, 3D, or sound design.
Experience working in agile, distributed, and multidisciplinary teams.
Meet your team
Join SAP's Enterprise AI CoE, where we shape, govern, and scale AI across the enterprise. We drive the adoption of leading AI solutions, empower colleagues worldwide, and set the standard for responsible, enterprise-ready AI.
Portfolio Expectations
The portfolio should show the candidate’s individual contribution and decision-making, not only the final visual output. Strong case studies will explain the problem, the design process, key trade-offs, collaboration with the wider team, and the impact of the work. Examples involving complex workflows, enterprise products, AI experiences, motion design, or design systems are especially relevant.
Bring out your best
SAP innovations help more than four hundred thousand customers worldwide work together more efficiently and use business insight more effectively. Originally known for leadership in enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, SAP has evolved to become a market leader in end-to-end business application software and related services for database, analytics, intelligent technologies, and experience management. As a cloud company with two hundred million users and more than one hundred thousand employees worldwide, we are purpose-driven and future-focused, with a highly collaborative team ethic and commitment to personal development. Whether connecting global industries, people, or platforms, we help ensure every challenge gets the solution it deserves. At SAP, you can bring out your best.
We win with inclusion
SAP’s culture of inclusion, focus on health and well-being, and flexible working models help ensure that everyone – regardless of background – feels included and can run at their best. At SAP, we believe we are made stronger by the unique capabilities and qualities that each person brings to our company, and we invest in our employees to inspire confidence and help everyone realize their full potential. We ultimately believe in unleashing all talent and creating a better world.

title: Product Designer
description:
OVERVIEW OF THE COMPANY
Fox Corporation Under the FOX banner, we produce and distribute content through some of the world’s leading and most valued brands, including: FOX News Media, FOX Sports, FOX Entertainment, FOX Television Stations and Tubi Media Group. We empower a diverse range of creators to imagine and develop culturally significant content, while building an organization that thrives on creative ideas, operational expertise and strategic thinking.
JOB DESCRIPTION
Supercast powers premium subscriptions for the world’s top podcasts and creators. We help creators like Huberman Lab, This American Life, Peter Attia, and My Favorite Murder build direct relationships with their audiences and generate recurring revenue through exclusive content and community.
Following our recent acquisition by Red Seat Ventures (a Fox Corp. company), Supercast is entering a new phase of product investment and expansion. Building on our success with podcast subscriptions, we’re evaluating a broader toolkit for podcast-first creators, as well as new ways for creators to engage and monetize their audiences.
About The Role
We’re looking for our first full-time Product Designer, reporting to the CEO, to help shape this next chapter. You’ll work closely with the Product Lead and Engineering team to design the experiences used by thousands of creators and hundreds of thousands of paying subscribers. Your work will define how creators launch, grow, and run subscription businesses on Supercast and how fans discover and engage with the content they love.
We believe the next generation of media companies will be creator-led, and our mission is to build the operating system for creator-led media businesses.
A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILTIES
Design the creator and subscriber experiences across the Supercast platform including the creator dashboard, subscriber interface, web application, mobile experiences, and supercast.com.
Own the UX, look, feel, and interactions of Supercast as the platform evolves and new capabilities are introduced.
Create the design system, UI designs, interaction flows, and prototypes that help the team move quickly from concept to shipped product.
Level up existing product flows to make launching and managing memberships simpler and more intuitive for creators.
Design entirely new product capabilities from scratch as Supercast expands into areas like mobile apps, livestreaming, community features, and other creator tools.
Partner closely with the Product Manager and Engineering team to translate product ideas into thoughtful user experiences, including refining UI and HTML/CSS details.
WHAT YOU WILL NEED
Product design experience. 4+ years designing digital products, ideally in SaaS, consumer platforms, or creator tools.
Strong UX intuition. You’re able to simplify complex workflows and design experiences that feel intuitive and delightful.
Customer empathy. You care deeply about understanding how creators and subscribers behave and design solutions that solve real user problems.
Design systems thinking. You’ve built and maintained Figma design systems before and lead with patterns, hierarchies and components.
Collaboration.You enjoy working efficiently with product managers and engineers to turn ideas into shipped product.
Craft. You sweat the details of UI, interaction design, and visual polish, including using AI thoughtfully in your design workflow
Front-end awareness. Comfort working with HTML/CSS and collaborating closely with engineers on implementation (we’re a Ruby on Rails shop using Tailwind).
Passion for the creator economy. You’re excited about building tools that empower creators to build sustainable businesses with their audiences.
We’re especially interested in candidates who have built products used by creators, media companies, or subscription businesses.
How We Measure Success
A delightful creator and subscriber experience.

title: Product Design Fellow
description:
Product Design Fellow
The Short Version
You’ll design products that don’t exist yet for founders building companies that don’t exist yet. Not redesigns. Not portfolio polish. Interfaces that didn’t have a user yesterday and need a thousand happy ones by next quarter.
What Liminal Is
A Founders' Studio. We co-build with repeat founders, many of them unicorn founders, providing build expertise, capital, and unfair access from founding to Series B. We call ourselves a Founders' Studio because “venture studio” undersells what we do and oversells what most of them deliver.
What This Role Actually Is
Product design at zero-to-one is applied behavioral science. You’re the person who catches why one onboarding flow converts and another bleeds users at step three, clocks why Linear’s keyboard shortcuts feel inevitable before everyone else copies them, and understands at a cellular level why some products feel like a thought finishing itself and others feel like work.
You’ll embark on projects with our Founders, designing the first user-facing surface of a venture from a blank Figma file: information architecture, interaction model, visual system, micro-interactions, copy. You’ll get range across industries before you specialise – different ventures, different users, different problem spaces. You partner with engineers to ship, but pretending to be one isn’t the job. Product thinking and craft first.
The Work
Product thinking and architecture. Build the structural foundation of a venture’s product: information hierarchy, user flows, mental models, edge cases. The skeleton every later pixel hangs on.
Interaction and interface. Wireframes, prototypes, polished UI. Real design work. Precise, considered, opinionated. A flow that makes a user say “oh, of course.” A first-time experience that gets to value in ninety seconds.
Research and synthesis. Run user interviews, usability sessions, and competitive teardowns. Turn what you hear into a point of view, not a transcript dump. Personas grounded in observed behavior, not personas in name only.
Microcopy and content design. The button label, the empty state, the error message. The places where most products give up and where the good ones quietly win.
Design systems and craft. Build the system that lets a small team move fast without things going sideways. Spacing, type, color, components – internally consistent, externally invisible.
Who You Are
Deep product literacy. We don’t care about your degree (or if you have one). We care if you can explain why Linear’s onboarding works, why Notion’s empty state is doing more work than people realize, and what Stripe and Things 3 have in common despite serving completely different jobs.
Exquisite taste. Not good taste. Exquisite. The kind where a two-pixel misalignment ruins your afternoon. Where you have opinions about loading spinners. Where you can articulate why an interaction feels right three beats before anyone else in the room catches up.
Strategic clarity. You can take a founder’s 45-minute monologue about a problem and ship a clickable prototype that makes them say “yes, exactly that.”
Comfort with ambiguity. Zero-to-one environments. No existing user base. No analytics dashboard. No design system to inherit. A founder with a world-changing obsession and a blank Figma file. That should thrill you, not paralyze you.
Contrarian streak. Independent thinker. Arguments from first principles. Unafraid of unpopular positions. You believe the best designs survive open critique. You know how to disagree and commit.
Early-career, high-trajectory. One to three years of work behind you – agency, in-house, startup, consultancy, or your own project. We care about evidence of work you’ve shipped, not titles you’ve held. Figma fluency assumed.
Unicorn Points If
You have serious industrial design and mechanical engineering chops. You’ve logged 2000+ hours on CAD and can also prototype in code. You read your own React, even if you don’t ship it. Also points if you have a research-deep background: cognitive science, behavioral economics, ethnography. Bonus, not the job. But if you can move fluidly between AutoCAD, Figma, and a working prototype while including a brief commentary on how the design is anti-brutalist without a handoff, you become unreasonably dangerous.
Fellowship, not internship
Twelve months. Meaningful stipend. Embedded in a core project alongside experienced builders. Not fetching coffee, that’s the leaders’ job. Not watching from the mezzanine. If you’ve been looking for a way into startup life or zero-to-one product design at the earliest stage, this is the door.

title: Product Designer
description:
In just over two years, we’ve gone from 0 to over 750 customers, succeeding where many have tried and failed before. We have a big mission: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run and grow a renewables installation business – and through that to make a massive dent in the world’s carbon emissions and create a hugely better experience for homeowners.
We’re now looking for a stellar Product Designer who’s buzzing to create exceptional experiences for installers as we expand into new markets.
🌲 About Spruce
Almost 20% of the UK’s carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there’s simply no way to make reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can’t currently offer a heat pump when someone’s boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.
We’re fixing this. We’ve built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we’re having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.
We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and have been scaling the team to massively grow our impact. We’re in the process of expanding outside heat pumps and by the end of the year will be an operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and autoCAD, you might get a sense of where we’re headed…
🥖 The Role
You’ll be central to our mission as we turn historically slow and painful processes into ones that are quick, intuitive and even delightful for installers. We’ve been design-led since the beginning but the challenge is only growing as our product becomes (necessarily) more complex. Day-to-day you’ll be:
Making complex decisions feel effortless – Our platform handles everything from building physics calculations to fluid dynamics modelling to complicated compliance requirements. We need to make handling that complexity feel effortless for all our customers, irrespective of how tech-savvy they are.
Designing across multiple touchpoints – You'll work on desktop design tools, homeowner-facing outputs, enquiry flows, mobile survey apps (incl LiDAR), and collaborative workflows that work seamlessly across different user types (from 3-person local installers to national utilities);
Collaborating closely with developers & shipping code yourself – Understanding data structures and technical constraints so your designs can be shipped quickly; and shipping PRs yourself when it makes sense (with the support of the dev team);
Building systematic, scalable design systems – Creating robust, structured, and reusable components that work across platforms and for potentially low-tech users;
Researching and validating - Interviewing and spending time with installers to deeply understand how they work and what the core problems to solve are; and building quick prototypes to test and validate design decisions and uncover unexpected pain points.
You'll report directly to Steph, our Co-Founder and CPO.
🫵 About You
We’re looking for a designer with
3+ years of product/UI design experience
(and potentially a lot more), ideally in a startup context or within fast-paced, impact-focussed teams. We'd love to speak with you if you are:
A clear, systematic thinker who loves tackling complex flows;
Comfortable with diving into technical detail, even if it’s a new domain;
User-obsessed; you enjoy deeply understanding the user, solving their problems and making a tangible impact on them;
Great with people and confident running research with customers;
Proactive and self-organising, happy juggling multiple projects;
Bonus if you’ve worked on tools for field teams, low-tech users, or on operational workflows (but absolutely not a requirement!).
🌟 Our offer
💰 £60-110k salary, depending on experience.
🍰 Meaningful slice of equity (options) in the company
🏖️ 33 days holiday and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year
🏡 Hybrid working: 2–3 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight
🏥 Private Medical Cover
👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme (YellowNest)
🚲 Cycle to Work scheme
👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow
🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce
We’re currently a close-knit team of 28, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2-3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone altogether every fortnight.
You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.
We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then be able to rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions. This is clearly particularly important for this role but you’ll be surrounded by a whole team who are also close to our customers.
We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it, what can we learn and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back.
Feedback is constant, direct, and kind – we'll tell you when something isn't working and expect the same honesty (and empathy) back.
Compensation Range: £60K - £110K

title: UI/UX Designer
description:
Build products that dental labs are excited to use.
On-site | Vancouver Office – 675 W Hastings St.
The Problem We're Solving
Dental labs and clinics across 28 countries run on fragmented workflows — disconnected communication and manual case management. EviSmart is replacing that with an intelligent, unified platform. The products are live and growing. What we need now is someone who understands the end users, learns how they really work, and turns that into an experience built for them.
Why EviSmart
300 people. Two hubs: Vancouver HQ and Manila operations.
145% year-over-year SaaS growth — the market is responding.
28 countries. One platform. The dental industry's Autopilot.
An in-house AI model research and development team building proprietary intelligence.
Why This Role, Right Now
EviSmart's product is expanding across several surfaces at once — a structured communication platform pulling labs and dentists off informal messaging channels, an AI-powered design module automating crown production, and a unified operations dashboard where it all comes together. As more of that UI gets built quickly — including with AI tools — the team needs someone embedded with them who keeps the experience usable and coherent, and who stays close to how dental labs actually work.
A Note from the Team
"We need someone who doesn't wait for a brief to start understanding the problem. They get in front of users, find where the experience breaks, and bring back something better. If you've done your best work in environments where the problem wasn't fully defined when you arrived, this is the right conversation."
— Paolo Kalaw, CEO, EviSmart
What
You’ll
Own
Usability testing and real time with users — run sessions and interviews with dentists and dental lab teams, and turn what you learn into design changes. You decide who you need to talk to; the sales and customer teams help you reach them.
Design for the surfaces the team is shipping — the mobile-first communication experience dentists use in the field, and the operations dashboard lab owners use to run daily workflow. Design for distinct user types without muddling the experience.
Take work from concept through to dev-ready design, working alongside the product team and engineers.
Design the UX of AI-assisted workflows — interfaces where AI output meets a human decision, built so users trust what they're seeing rather than second-guess it.
What You'll Get
Real influence over an experience thousands of dental labs use every day
Direct access to 2,000+ real lab customers for user research — the feedback loop is fast and the stakes are real.
AI-native product work from day one — designing interfaces where model output meets user decision-making
Production AI tooling built in-house: Claude, Cursor, and LLM-powered workflows — not a sandbox, not a pilot.
Competitive compensation: $80,000–$100,000 CAD (depending on experience)
How We Work
We ship before we’re 100% certain. We write things down because we have two offices and memory is lossy. We debate loudly and move without resentment. We treat the customer’s real problem as more important than an elegant internal process. If you’ve spent time waiting for permission to try something obvious — you’ll notice the difference here immediately.
What We Need
3–4 years of product or UX design experience with complex, workflow-heavy, or operational products — B2B SaaS with non-technical end users is a strong plus.
You've run usability testing and talked to users yourself. You've sat with users, seen where they get stuck, and changed your designs because of it.
You can take a project from rough concept to dev-ready specs and work well with engineers to ship it.
Strong in Figma, wireframing, prototyping, and interaction design — across both mobile and desktop.
A clear communicator who can present work and take pushback from PMs, engineers, and execs without losing composure.
You've designed for multiple distinct user types within the same product without muddling the experience.
You think about how design affects whether users adopt and stick with a product — not just how it looks.
Comfortable working in AI-assisted design workflows (Figma, Claude, Cursor).
Apply today @ EviSmart Careers

description:
DeepLight AI is a specialist AI and data consultancy dedicated to transforming the regional corporate landscape through bespoke, high-impact intelligent systems. We deliver tailored AI solutions designed to integrate seamlessly into existing enterprise architectures, ensuring that innovation is both scalable and secure. From building robust data foundations to deploying sophisticated AI platforms, we empower our clients to lead in an increasingly automated world.
On a data platform, the thing under test
is
the data. As a QA Engineer, you own how we prove our platforms work end to end - from the pipelines that move and transform data to the API layers that expose it. This is a verification role: you don't build the pipelines, you build the confidence that they are correct.
You won't just be "checking boxes"; you will be thinking critically about how data flows from source to insight and out to the consumer, ensuring every transformation and every endpoint maintains the integrity required for high-stakes financial services environments.
Your responsibilities as a QA Engineer include;
Designing, building, and owning automated test suites - functional, integration, and end-to-end - embedded into CI so quality gates run continuously
Testing the platform's API layer through contract testing, schema validation, and end-to-end checks against externally-consumed and partner-facing data APIs
Performing rigorous source-to-target reconciliation and checksums to ensure no "silent failures" occur during complex AWS Glue or Data Factory transformations
Extending and running Soda Core checks across Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers, and verifying that quality gates fire correctly as part of your automated suites
Monitoring automated alerts, performing initial root-cause analysis on data drift or schema failures, and collaborating with squads to implement permanent countermeasures
Working alongside Data Engineering squads to embed automated validation into live data flows, and supporting the data contracts and OpenMetadata lineage that producers and consumers rely on
As an AI consultancy, our greatest asset is the expertise of our people. While technical mastery is the foundation of what we do, the ability to bridge the gap between complex data engineering and actionable business value is what defines your success with Deeplight. We're looking for individuals who are not only world-class in their fields of specialism, but also compelling communicators and persuasive advocates for their own skills. You will be the face of our firm, tasked with building trust, articulating the "why" behind your technical decisions, and effectively "selling" your vision to high-level stakeholders. If you thrive on the challenge of presenting cutting-edge solutions as much as you do on building them, you will fit right in.
Requirements
What we need from you:
2-4 years of experience in QA / test automation, ideally on data-intensive or backend platforms
Strong proficiency in SQL and Python for test automation, data validation, and scripting
Practical experience with API and contract testing (e.g. REST, schema/contract validation)
Hands-on experience designing and maintaining automated test frameworks and CI-embedded suites
Practical understanding of Lakehouse architectures and the Medallion (Bronze/Silver/Gold) design pattern
Hands-on experience with AWS services (specifically S3, Glue, and Athena) or similar cloud data stacks
A degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, or a related field
The ability to look beyond a failed check to understand the root cause and its broader business impact
An uncompromising eye for accuracy, ensuring referential integrity, reconciliation, and checksums are perfectly aligned
Comfortable working in fast-paced environments using Jira and participating actively in Scrum ceremonies
The ability to communicate technical issues clearly and constructively, fostering a culture of quality within the engineering team
It would also be great if you have:
Experience testing externally-consumed or partner-facing APIs, particularly in regulated data-sharing contexts
Hands-on exposure to data-quality tooling such as Soda Core or equivalents
Prior exposure to OpenMetadata or other lineage and metadata management tools
A proactive drive to identify repetitive tasks and develop scripts to increase team efficiency
Familiarity with the specific data challenges found within the Financial Services or Banking sectors
Benefits
The benefits you'll enjoy as part of this role include:
Competitive salary
Comprehensive personal health insurance
Visa Sponsorship for the successful individual
Professional development and certification support
Subscription reimbursement relating to your role
Opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI projects

The Software Quality Engineer is responsible for improving and ensuring software quality, stability and release confidence by validating customer workflows, identifying risks, collaborating with Product and Engineering teams, and applying effective testing strategies across software applications.
This role plays a critical part in testing new features, performing exploratory testing, and ensuring that test coverage meets business and technical requirements. With a primary focus in manual testing, this role will also perform basic automation scripting for regression testing in order to improve efficiency where necessary.
Our tech stack includes HTML5/CSS, Node.js, React, TypeScript, C#, Python, JavaScript, Docker, AWS, and Azure Services, along with databases such as MS-SQL, PostgreSQL, and Snowflake.

:

Manual Testing Execution: Perform functional, exploratory, regression, and user acceptance testing to validate software functionality.

Bug Tracking & Reporting: Identify, document, and prioritize defects, providing detailed reports to developers to ensure timely fixes.
Cross-Browser and Device Testing: Ensure applications work across different devices, browsers including Edge, Chrome, Firefox and others, and operating systems such as Windows & MacOS.
End-to-End Testing: Validate end-to-end customer workflows, data integrity, integrations, business rules, and data flows across connected systems.
Automation for Regression Coverage: Contribute to automation coverage by identifying opportunities where automation provides meaningful value and maintaining reliable automated tests that improve testing efficiency.
Collaboration with Developers: Work closely with software engineers to reproduce issues and verify fixes.

Work Closely with Product and Engineering Teams: Understand business requirements and acceptance criteria to create effective test cases.
Improve Testing Strategies: Identify opportunities for improving manual testing efficiency and propose automation where beneficial.
Maintain Testing Documentation: Keep detailed records of test cases, results, and defect reports.

title: QA Engineer
description:
About The Job
Our mission
Boom is on a mission to level the playing field for the 110+ million renters in the US by making housing more flexible, affordable, and rewarding. Boom is building a suite of rental financial services for renters and property managers, including tenant screening, rent payment reporting, rent reporting-as-a-service, and a number of integrations with the largest property management systems (PMS). Boom serves renters through the Boom App and property managers via the Boom Platform. Now serving thousands of renters, Boom is led by second-time founder Rob Whiting (ex-BCG, Rubicon). It's backed by investors such as Starting Line, Clocktower Ventures, Gilgamesh Ventures (Petal co-founders), and angels such as William Hockey and Zach Perret (Co-founders of Plaid) and Harry Stebbings. Boom has been profiled by Inman, Business Insider, HousingWire, and more.
Opportunity
The QA Engineer owns product quality, reliability, and consistency across the Boom platform. You'll run manual and exploratory testing, identify bugs, and verify quality across web, mobile, and our integrations, with a focus on customer impact, edge cases, and release readiness.
At Boom, quality directly affects property manager trust and renter experience. A payment that fails, a report that breaks, or a workflow that confuses users erodes confidence fast. You'll partner closely with product, engineering, and customer success to catch issues before they reach customers, document clean reproduction steps, and advocate for the fixes that matter most.
This is a hands-on testing role for someone who enjoys breaking things to make them better and thrives in a fast-paced environment. For this role, we are hiring for candidates in Austin, TX, where our leadership and product team is located. Comp range listed is directional and adjustable +/- based on competency.
What You'll Do
Run manual and exploratory testing across new features, regressions, and edge cases. Validate behavior across browsers, operating systems, and mobile devices
Test third-party integrations (payment processors, accounting systems, banking partners) for data accuracy and reliability
Own final QA sign-off for production releases. Critical paths work or we don't ship
Maintain regression suites and catch unintended side effects from new code or config changes
Write clear, reproducible bug reports with screenshots, repro steps, expected vs actual behavior, and severity. Verify fixes in staging and production
Partner with PMs and engineers to clarify requirements, reproduce issues, and ship customer-focused tests grounded in real user workflows
Maintain test cases, checklists, and QA standards so quality holds up as we scale
What You'll Need
2+ years of QA or software testing experience, ideally on web and mobile in SaaS or fintech
Strong analytical instincts. You assess product behavior beyond the documented acceptance criteria and proactively clarify requirements when they're vague or incomplete
Clean, structured bug reports are second nature: repro steps, screenshots, severity, expected vs actual
Comfortable with browser dev tools, network inspection, basic debugging, and API integration testing
Daily use of AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) for test case generation, exploratory testing, and scripting. We use AI heavily across the team and expect new hires to do the same
Balance thoroughness with speed in a fast-moving startup environment
Strong written communicator who collaborates cross-functionally with product and engineering
Plus: experience testing payment flows, financial systems, or compliance-sensitive features; exposure to test automation or scripting
Empathy for our end users, including low-to-moderate-income renters, and a desire to build products that make a difference
Benefits Of Working At Boom
Competitive salary with stock options
Full healthcare coverage (health, dental, vision) including 50% coverage for dependents
15 days of Paid Time Off (PTO) per year + 3 sick days + all US federal holidays (11 in total) (note: we think unlimited PTO is BS and causes some employees to feel guilty when they take it)
Company-issued laptop/MacBook
Company-sponsored training & development
Regular off-sites, retreats, and other company-sponsored events and travel opportunities

title: Quality Assurance Engineer
description:
About Rune
Rune Technologies builds mission-critical software for military logistics and sustainment. Our flagship product is TyrOS, an AI-enabled logistics command and control platform that gives commanders a single, real-time operating picture of their sustainment fight, from inventory and distribution to medical and operational planning, even in degraded and contested environments.
We're not a traditional defense contractor. We're a small, fast-moving team that combines deep operational experience in and with the DoD with the software discipline of the best product companies, and we apply that combination to a customer set that desperately needs it. We stay close to our users by embedding directly with military units during exercises and rotations, and we ship constantly based on what we learn.
The U.S. military and its allies face a real logistics modernization problem. We're building the software to solve it.
About The Role
At Rune Technologies, we are building the logistics technology backbone that the U.S. and allied militaries need to dominate in large-scale combat operations. As a Quality Assurance Engineer at Rune, you will play a critical role in ensuring the reliability, stability, and quality of the software that supports mission-critical logistics operations for the warfighter.
You'll join us in our mission to bring 21st-century software to the sustainment domain—modernizing inventory management, transportation optimization, and predictive maintenance with state-of-the-art user experiences. You'll work closely with software engineers, product leaders, Mission Managers, and TechOps to ensure every release of TyrOS meets the quality standards our customers depend on in operational environments.
This is Rune's first dedicated Quality Assurance role. Rather than inheriting an established QA organization, you'll build one. You'll define testing processes, develop scalable automation, and become the quality gatekeeper for our engineering team. If you enjoy creating systems from the ground up, thrive in fast-moving startup environments, and want to directly influence how software is built and released, we'd love to talk to you.
What You'll Do
Own quality across the TyrOS software development lifecycle, ensuring new features meet our quality standards before reaching production.
Review every pull request destined for the main branch by validating testing evidence, spinning up ephemeral environments, verifying functionality, and approving or blocking releases.
Build, maintain, and expand our Playwright end-to-end test suite covering critical user workflows across TyrOS.
Design automated tests that reduce manual regression testing and improve engineering velocity over time.
Execute release regression testing to ensure production readiness before every software release.
Perform non-functional testing including performance validation, accessibility testing, data integrity verification, and basic load testing.
Partner with software engineers during feature planning to review acceptance criteria, identify testing strategies, and determine which automated checks should block releases.
Collaborate with Mission Managers and Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) to validate customer-specific deployments, upgrade paths, and operational workflows.
Establish QA metrics, documentation, testing standards, and repeatable processes that scale alongside our engineering organization.
Continuously improve our testing strategy through automation, tooling, and process improvements.
Qualifications
2+ years of Quality Assurance, Test Automation, or Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) experience supporting modern web applications.
Hands-on experience with Playwright or a comparable end-to-end testing framework such as Cypress or Selenium.
Experience building and maintaining automated testing suites.
Comfortable reading application code to understand changes and validate testing coverage. Familiarity with Go and/or TypeScript/React is a strong plus.
Strong understanding of regression testing methodologies and release validation.
Ability to work independently and establish processes in a fast-paced startup environment.
Excellent written communication skills, including bug reports, test documentation, and QA metrics.
Strong collaboration skills with engineers and cross-functional partners throughout the software development lifecycle.
Desired Qualifications
Experience working in defense technology, government software, or other highly regulated industries.
Familiarity with GitHub Actions and CI/CD pipelines.
Experience working with Kubernetes-based deployment environments.
Experience performing accessibility, performance, and load testing.
Experience validating APIs and backend services.
Benefits
Rune offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees to include a full suite of insurance options at no cost for employees and low-cost to spouses and dependents. Highly competitive equity grants are also included in the majority of full time offers and are considered part of Rune's total compensation package. Benefits include:
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans; premiums 100% covered by Rune for all employees; exceptionally low premiums for spouses and dependents
Basic life insurance and disability 100% covered for all employees by Rune; option to purchase additional life insurance available
‘Take the time off that you need, when you need it’ paid time off, not accrual based
Generous company holiday calendar including a holiday shutdown in December
Supportive leave of absence program including time off for military service, medical events, and parental leave
Full 401(k) retirement plan for all full-time eligible employees
Company-funded commuter benefits
Free access to on-site gym at office

title: Quality Assurance Engineer
description:
About Boost Payment Solutions
Boost Payment Solutions is transforming B2B payments through secure, cloud-native platforms for payment processing, payment facilitation, settlement, and enterprise payment workflows. Our technology moves mission-critical financial transactions where reliability, accuracy, and security are non-negotiable.
About the Role
You will join a Quality Engineering function that is being rebuilt, not maintained.
We are migrating an existing Selenium suite to Playwright, standing up scenario-first regression coverage across Gen-3 payment processing, email and file parsing, and PayFac settlement, and wiring it into GitHub Actions so quality signal appears on every pull request. You will write automation daily, use AI tooling to accelerate test creation and migration, and own real coverage on a platform that processes live money.
If you are looking for a mature suite to maintain, this is not that role. If you want to build one, it is.
Why this role matters
You own measurable regression coverage on mission-critical B2B payment flows — not a slice of someone else’s suite.
You work across the full stack of quality signal: UI, API, database validation, and CI pipeline health.
You use AI tooling in production practice, not as an experiment — with review standards that keep it trustworthy.
What You’ll Do
Automation & Framework Contribution
Build and maintain automated tests in our Playwright framework across UI, API, and end-to-end suites.
Contribute to the Selenium-to-Playwright migration using AI-assisted tooling (Kiro), reviewing all generated output before merge.
Keep tests running in GitHub Actions — improving stability, execution speed, and reporting while retiring flaky and low-value tests.
Follow the scenario-first design standard: one scenario, one fixed assertion set, so a failure names itself without an SME.
Test Execution, Coverage & Traceability
Execute functional, integration, end-to-end, and regression testing across payment processing, parsing, and settlement workflows.
Write and maintain test cases in AIO Test with traceability to Jira stories, acceptance criteria, automation, and defects.
Validate data end to end — write SQL against Postgres schemas to confirm parsing, enrichment, and reconciliation results, not just UI state.
Build regression coverage for high-volume email and file ingestion, payment APIs, and third-party integrations.
AI-Assisted Quality Engineering
Use AI tooling to generate, refactor, and maintain automated tests, test data scenarios, and failure analysis.
Review every AI-generated test for correctness, coverage, edge cases, security, and maintainability before it lands.
Operate within Boost’s AI usage, data-handling, and code review standards — no production or cardholder data in AI tooling.
Share what works and what doesn’t, so practice improves for the whole team rather than one engineer.
Release Quality, Environments & Reporting
Support release quality gates and promotion decisions with Engineering and DevOps, including evidence capture for each gate.
Apply repeatable test data and environment readiness practices — synthetic data, reusable accounts, controlled datasets, and refresh procedures.
Report quality metrics in binary terms: automation coverage, pass rate, defect leakage, and regression health — with numerator and denominator, not narrative.
Join backlog refinement, sprint planning, and release readiness reviews to surface coverage gaps and integration risk early.
What You Bring
Required
3–5 years in Quality Engineering, Test Automation, or Software QA, with hands-on automation delivery in Agile or DevOps environments.
Working experience with Playwright, Cypress, or Selenium across UI, API, and end-to-end automation.
Proficiency in Python and/or TypeScript sufficient to write and maintain automation code independently. (Java, C#, or JavaScript backgrounds considered where the fundamentals are strong.)
Ability to write SQL for data validation — joins, aggregates, and result comparison against expected datasets.
Experience running automated tests in GitHub Actions or a comparable CI/CD pipeline.
Experience testing APIs, integrations, or cloud-native applications, and comfort reading logs to diagnose a failure before escalating it.
Clear written communication — able to state a quality risk in terms of business impact.
Preferred
Payments, fintech, banking, or PCI-regulated experience — settlement, funding, tokenization, or transaction platforms.
High-volume data ingestion or parsing validation (email, EDI, batch file, or similar structured feeds).
AWS experience — S3, Secrets Manager, Step Functions, or equivalent cloud-native testing exposure.
Hands-on use of AI-assisted tools for test creation, maintenance, or failure analysis.
Test management tooling (AIO Test, Xray, Zephyr), and experience working with distributed or offshore teams.
What we use
Automation
Playwright (migrating from Selenium) · Python · TypeScript
API & data
REST Assured / Postman · SQL against Postgres · S3 · Snowflake (in progress)
CI/CD
GitHub Actions — PR smoke gate, nightly full regression, post-deploy production smoke
Test management
AIO Test (Jira-native) · Jira · Confluence for strategy and evidence
AI tooling
Kiro for spec-driven test generation and Selenium-to-Playwright migration
Cloud
AWS — S3, Secrets Manager, Step Functions
What Success Looks Like in Your First Year
-
Area Expected impact
Coverage
Reliable automated coverage across the critical workflows, APIs, and integrations you own.
Speed
Tests run in CI on every PR and nightly
Traceability
Your test cases map cleanly to Jira stories, automation, and defects.
AI leverage
A meaningful share of your test creation and maintenance is AI-accelerated and reviewed to standard.
Our Hiring Process
Recruiter conversation — role, background, and logistics.
Hiring manager screen — your hands-on automation experience, in specifics.
Practical exercise — you will review an existing automated test, identify what is wrong with it, and propose improvements. We care how you think about test design, not whether you memorized syntax.
Team interview — collaboration with Engineering, Product, and DevOps.
Why Boost
Direct impact on platform reliability, release confidence, and customer experience on live payment rails.
A quality function with executive sponsorship and a funded roadmap — not an afterthought.
Real exposure to cloud-native platforms, AI-enabled engineering practice, and modern delivery models.
Room to grow into senior quality engineering work as the function scales.
Compensation & equal opportunity
Base salary range: $140,000– $150,000, plus bonus and benefits. Final offer reflects experience, skills, and location.
Boost Payment Solutions is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

title: QA Tester Intern — AI-Assisted Testing and Automation
description:

Company: Elchai Group
Location: Dubai, UAE, on-site
Department: Product, Engineering, and Quality Assurance
Type: internship, Monday to Friday, 10 to 4, eight to twelve weeks
Compensation: unpaid, with a completion certificate subject to satisfactory performance
Future opportunity: high-performing interns may be considered for a paid role based on performance and company needs
About the role:
Elchai Group builds advanced digital platforms across AI infrastructure, real-world assets, legal AI, compliance-focused workflows, investor portals, and admin dashboards. These are complex, multi-step business systems, not simple websites. We are also building a voice-first AI business assistant that team members use through both a desktop and a browser app, so this role now includes testing spoken AI interactions as well. We are looking for a QA Tester Intern to help test all of these platforms before they reach users, investors, internal teams, and partners.
This role suits someone who wants practical experience in software testing, QA automation, AI-assisted testing, Playwright, API testing, voice interface testing, and product quality. This is not a basic manual testing internship. You should be willing to learn how to test complex products, including an AI voice assistant, using structured QA thinking, AI tools, browser testing, and clear documentation.
Key responsibilities:
Use AI tools to help generate and organize test cases, edge cases, and regression checklists.
Run manual and exploratory testing across dashboards, portals, admin panels, and user flows like sign-up, login, onboarding, forms, approvals, uploads, and downloads.
Check error, loading, and empty states, mobile responsiveness, and cross-browser behavior.
Support Playwright automation for login flows, form validation, role-based access, and multi-step workflows.
Test APIs and backend workflows, including response status, authentication, permissions, data consistency, and audit logs.
Perform boundary testing to confirm what the system should not allow, such as a normal user reaching admin pages or seeing another user's private records.
Test the voice assistant, including whether it correctly hears speech in multi languages, whether it speaks answers back cleanly, and whether interruption and resume behave properly.
Test AI answer quality, including whether the assistant grounds its answers in the correct documents, whether it avoids making things up, and whether it stays within its rules.
Test document upload and retrieval, confirming that an uploaded file is read correctly and can be found in later answers.
Test data isolation, confirming that one person's private conversations and data never appear in another person's session.
Write clear, reproducible bug reports developers can act on quickly.
We ask for discretion and care with confidential project material.
Requirements:
Strong interest in QA, software testing, AI tools, and automation.
Basic understanding of web applications.
Good attention to detail.
Clear written English for reports and documentation.
The ability to read product requirements and turn them into test cases.
Basic knowledge of JavaScript or TypeScript.
Basic understanding of Playwright, or willingness to learn quickly.
Familiarity with browser DevTools.
The ability to test both successful and failure flows, hands-on.
Nice to have:
Playwright, Cypress, or Postman.
REST API testing.
GitHub or GitHub Actions.
Basic SQL.
Tools like Jira, Linear, or Trello.
Figma inspection, accessibility testing, or security testing basics.
Prompt or LLM testing.
Interest in AI voice products, fintech, legaltech, regtech, SaaS, or investor platforms.
What you'll learn:
AI-assisted QA workflows.
Playwright automation.
Manual and exploratory testing.
API and UI testing.
Voice and AI assistant testing.
QA documentation and bug triage.
Test planning from product requirements.
How to test complex investor, compliance, and admin platforms.
How to work with developers, product managers, and operations teams.
Ideal candidate:
Not someone who waits for instructions every minute. We need someone structured, detail-oriented, curious, and quick to learn, who can test complex workflows carefully, including an AI voice assistant. Read a requirement, design the tests, find what breaks, and document it clearly.
This suits an early-career candidate aiming to become a QA automation engineer, AI QA tester, product QA analyst, or software tester.
